root_cause.trace: submit_work never had a resource-constraint parameter at all -- 'no paid resources' was a certification-process constraint on how the human/session chose to run a canary, never threaded into submit_work, the Proposal dataclass, studio_router.rank(), or evolution/advance.py._implementation_router(). Separately, route_preview and the real live router use genuinely different ranking logic: route_preview calls studio_router.rank() directly (locality/cost/risk score, which already puts free/local first by default), while the real live path (evolution/advance.py._implementation_router) takes rank()'s ACCEPTED candidates and re-orders them via its OWN duty-cycle evidence-based weighting (_rank_engineering_engines(), currently: claude_code duty=0.1 primary, omni_engineer duty=0.4 fallback) -- a deliberate, Founder-authorized 2026-08-19 correction, orthogonal to cost. Neither layer had ANY hard cost-based exclusion, so duty-cycle preference for claude_code could always win regardless of a cost/paid intent that was never actually expressed as data anywhere in the system.
root_cause.classification: constraint never existed in the schema (primary) + preview/live use different ranking algorithms with no shared hard-filter layer (secondary, now closed by the same fix)

fix.principle: Resource constraint enforced as a HARD ELIGIBILITY FILTER inside the one shared function both layers already call (studio_router.rank()), at the exact same tier as the existing allow_founder_gated filter -- not a new router, not a score, not a second implementation.
fix.studio_router.py: _evaluate()/rank()/select() gained allow_paid: bool = True. When False, any candidate whose cost_class's first word (the SAME parsing _score()/_COST_RANK already use) is 'metered_api' is rejected before scoring, with an explicit reason string. Default True preserves 100% of existing behavior for every current caller.
fix.evolution/proposal.py: Proposal gained paid_resources_allowed: bool = True (backward-compatible default for the ~9500 pre-existing proposals and the OBSERVE engine, neither of which ever declared this). create() gained a matching kwarg.
fix.evolution/advance.py: _implementation_router() gained allow_paid: bool = True, passed straight into studio_router.rank(). advance_one() threads it from the real proposal: allow_paid=getattr(p, 'paid_resources_allowed', True). _rank_engineering_engines() (the duty-cycle reorder) is UNCHANGED -- it still only ever reorders whatever rank() already accepted, which now correctly excludes paid candidates upstream when the proposal says so. No control-flow changes were needed in advance_one(): the pre-existing 'no engine completed cleanly this attempt' controlled-escalation path (proposal stays PROPOSED, retried up to MAX_IMPLEMENTATION_ATTEMPTS, then REJECTED with a clear reason -- never silently routed to a different engine) already does exactly the right thing once accepted_engines is correctly empty.
fix.services/th3_mcp/tools.py: submit_work gained paid_resources_allowed: bool = False (safe default at this external-facing entry point specifically -- the dataclass/create() default stays True for backward compatibility with internal callers). _first_pass_classify() now returns a distinct 'no_eligible_free_local_route' classification (not conflated with founder_gated) when a capable route exists ONLY via a paid provider; submit_work returns accepted=false with reason=NO_ELIGIBLE_FREE_LOCAL_ROUTE and creates NO Proposal in that case -- never silently falls through. route_preview gained the same paid_resources_allowed parameter (default True, preserving old callers), using the identical studio_router.rank(allow_paid=...) call, so preview and live can never disagree on the hard policy. work_result now surfaces the proposal's real paid_resources_allowed value.

why_this_is_not_always_omni_engineer_fir: The fix does not touch _rank_engineering_engines()'s evidence-based duty-cycle preference at all. When paid_resources_allowed=True (the default for internal/OBSERVE-origin proposals and any submit_work caller who explicitly opts in), claude_code remains the duty-preferred primary exactly as before -- proven by test_paid_resources_allowed_true_preserves_normal_duty_cycle_routing. The hard filter only ever removes a candidate from consideration entirely; it never re-orders the remaining ones.
